items.feedback_item: arm region [145.0, 680.0, 380.0, 835.0]: folding wheel arms rendered as short fixed brackets
items.must_change: The solution claims four folding aluminium wheel arms connecting the twin-tube chassis to the rigid grouser wheels to widen track for stow and stability. The render actually shows only short fixed vertical brackets above the wheels with no diagonal folding members, which contradicts the specified chassis-to-arm-to-wheel load path and the stowed 0.90 by 0.42 m envelope widening to 1.05 m length and 0.68 m track with 0.13 m side shift and 0.025 m rotation gap (E51). No change to the solution or whiteboard is required because arm count, function, material and stow/deploy geometry are already fixed, so the next render must draw the four diagonal arms per the sketch. This matters for deploying stability and box fit, but the mismatch says nothing about the design soundness.

items.feedback_item: callout [228.0, 503.0, 360.0, 625.0]: Narrow Kerf Chain leader ends on deck hoses
items.must_change: The solution claims a narrow kerf trenching chain cutting a 100 mm wide slot 50 mm deep with 11 N cut resistance feeding side spoil to the ladder (E64). The render actually places the leader on black hoses and cables on the chassis deck mid-frame, not on the vertical chain in the trench at bottom center. No change to the solution or whiteboard is required because the kerf part, its 50 to 100 mm size class, and its mechanical feed to the ladder are already fixed, so the leader must be redrawn to the chain in the trench. This matters for drawing readability, not for cutting or feeding function.

items.feedback_item: callout [735.0, 268.0, 868.0, 300.0]: Steep Wedge Hopper leader ends on soil stream
items.must_change: The solution claims a 20 L steep wedge hopper containing carried soil at 15 kg half-full trips up to 30 kg max (E10) with fill to 15 kg in 112 s (E11) and gravity chute feed from the ladder. The render actually ends the leader on the falling soil stream above the hopper, not on the hopper steel body. No change to the solution or whiteboard is required because the hopper part, its 150 to 450 mm size class, and its ladder-to-hopper gravity connection are already fixed and the latest render correctly shows the chute over the hopper with a functional gap, so the leader must be moved to the hopper body. This matters for part identification, not for containment.

items.feedback_item: callout [596.0, 605.0, 734.0, 637.0]: duplicate Tilt Screw Discharge labels misplaced
items.must_change: The solution claims a single tilt screw discharge metering 15 kg pours through the 150 mm outlet with pivot at 0.55 m clearing the 0.40 m lip by 0.15 m at tip safety factor 1.69 level-only (E51). The render actually shows two identical Tilt Screw Discharge labels with one ending on the hopper side panel and one near the outlet. No change to the solution or whiteboard is required because the screw part, its rear outlet location, and its hopper-to-auger metering connection are already fixed, so the duplicate must be removed and the single leader redrawn to the screw outlet at the hopper rear. This matters for discharge identification, not for metering function.

items.feedback_item: callout [15.0, 639.0, 148.0, 672.0]: duplicate Rigid Grouser Wheels labels, one on soil
items.must_change: The solution claims four rigid grouser wheels traversing loose soil with 294 N available traction against 11 N cut (E23) at 15.6 kPa ground pressure (E25) and brake-only stop in 0.0625 m (E23). The render actually shows two identical Rigid Grouser Wheels labels with the upper leader ending on the left soil pile, not on a wheel. No change to the solution or whiteboard is required because wheel count, 200 to 220 mm size class, grouser function and arm-to-wheel mounts are already fixed, so the duplicate must be removed and the single leader redrawn to a wheel. This matters for drawing clarity, not for traction or flotation.

items.feedback_item: battery [280.0, 580.0, 430.0, 630.0]: two lithium phosphate packs not identifiable
items.must_change: The solution claims two lithium phosphate battery packs on the chassis with fused bus to dig and drive and fused rails to cameras, closing the energy budget with 16.4 W ladder dig power (E59) and 0.512 Wh per trip (E60) and bounded motor heating rise of 18 K (E44). The render actually shows unlabeled black deck boxes and cables with no identifiable two packs. No change to the solution or whiteboard is required because pack count, chemistry, function and electrical connections to ladder and cameras are already fixed, so the next render must draw and label the two packs distinctly on the deck. This matters for power identification, but the unlabeled boxes say nothing about energy closure.

summary: DRAWING FAILURE after three rounds is a render fidelity limit, not a design verdict. All contested parts, connections and stow/deploy and clearance geometry are already specified on the board, and the chassis-ladder-hopper mounts plus gravity chute already match the sketch. No solution or whiteboard change is required.
